needs: right-operand reference to the requesting agent (rl2:rightOperandRef rl2:currentAgent): odrl:rightOperandReference is rejected, so the comparison of two runtime values is reduced to an assembler-computed boolean state property (due2-profiles.md §4)
notes: rl2:anyAgent becomes a permission without assignee. The RL2 condition asset.dataOwner eq rl2:currentAgent compares a state fact with the requester; due2 constraints compare one operand with authored values, and dprod:currentAgent cannot appear on the right. The policy therefore reads ex:requesterIsDataOwner, which the assembler derives by comparing the target's owner with the request subject. What is lost: the comparison moves out of the policy, and the assembler must propagate the owner fact's status — a conflicting owner assertion that disagrees on the requester becomes a conflict on the derived fact, a missing owner a missing derived fact. Under that assembler rule every RL2 outcome is reproduced. Scenario 4 is added.

expected.why: The assembler found asset.dataOwner = Alice = request subject, so the fact is true; ex:ownerPrivilege has no party to match, action and target match, and the constraint is T. Ready candidate.
Owner sources say Alice and Bob, so the derived fact is in conflict; the constraint and the permission are U. Completions give Permit and NotApplicable.
asset.dataOwner = Bob ≠ Alice, so the derived fact is false and the constraint F; the permission does not apply and nothing else does.
No owner is recorded, so the derived fact is missing and the constraint U; the permission is U and the completions give Permit and NotApplicable.
